subject: Clarify: volume breakpoints, on-demand overage & true-up process
messages:
From: Emily Carter <procurement@aurumhealth.com>
To: aditya_rao@redwood.com
Cc: Ben Torres <ben.torres@aurumhealth.com>
Date: Thu, 20 May 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Clarify: volume breakpoints, on-demand overage & true-up process

Hi Aditya,

Thanks for the demo yesterday — the team was impressed with Redwood's latency and the KV-cache savings. Before we move to a formal PO, procurement needs clarity on a few pricing mechanics so we can model our budget. High level: our initial usage profile is around 120M tokens/month (inference only). We expect spikes (product events) that could push us 2-3x for short windows.

Specific questions we need answered:
- Please show how your commit tiers & per-token discounts apply at 50M / 100M / 200M monthly commit breakpoints.
- What is the minimum monthly spend commitment for each tier? Do you bill a monthly minimum even if we underutilize?
- How are on-demand/burst tokens priced when we exceed the committed amount? Is there an overage per-token rate, and is that rate fixed or tiered?
- Do you offer a 'soft burst' buffer (a percentage of commit that can be used without immediate overage billing) and how is that reconciled at true-up?
- How does the true-up / quarterly reconciliation work (billing lag, credits, invoices)?

If you can provide a simple worked example for our expected profile (120M baseline; one event month at 300M), that would be ideal.

We're on a fairly typical procurement cadence: legal + security review, then PO and DocuSign. Happy to loop in more folks if needed.

Thanks,
Emily Carter
Procurement Lead
Aurum Health

--

From: aditya_rao@redwood.com
To: Emily Carter <procurement@aurumhealth.com>
Cc: Ben Torres <ben.torres@aurumhealth.com>, marissa_cole@redwood.com
Date: Fri, 21 May 2027 10:38:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Clarify: volume breakpoints, on-demand overage & true-up process

Hi Emily — great questions. I pulled together our standard approach plus a few concession options we can offer to match Aurum's profile. See the summary below and the attached worksheet for line-by-line math.

Summary (committed hosted API, per-token pricing):
- Commit tiers (monthly) - list price per generation token (USD):
  * 50M commit -> $0.00065/token
  * 100M commit -> $0.00055/token
  * 200M commit -> $0.00048/token
- Minimum monthly bill: equal to 75% of the monthly commit for contract year 1 (we can discuss 100% for longer terms). Example: 100M commit -> min bill = 75M tokens charged at commit rate.
- On-demand / overage pricing (tokens above monthly commit):
  * Default: on-demand = 2.0x committed rate (i.e., if commit rate $0.00055 -> on-demand $0.00110)
  * Alternative: capped burst pricing = 1.8x committed rate for first 20% of overage (soft-burst buffer), then default on-demand beyond that.
- Soft-burst buffer: we can provide a rolling 20% soft-burst (on top of commit) that is not invoiced immediately; instead, all burst consumption reconciled at quarterly true-up. At true-up we either bill or credit based on net usage vs committed volumes.
- True-up cadence and mechanics: quarterly reconciled on invoice following the quarter. If you underuse relative to billed minima, we'll credit next invoice. If you overuse, we'll invoice overage at the agreed on-demand rates; for promotional deals we can apply graduated step-downs.

Worked example (Aurum profile):
- Commit chosen: 100M/month (baseline) at $0.00055/token.
- Minimum monthly billed = 75M tokens -> $41,250/month.
- Month A (normal): 120M tokens consumed. Billing: 100M at commit rate ($55,000) + 20M overage at soft-burst policy. If we apply soft-burst (20% of commit = 20M), we defer immediate billing and reconcile at quarter end.
- Month B (event): 300M tokens consumed. Billing: 100M commit + 200M overage. First 20M of overage per month treated under soft-burst buffer (deferred); remaining 180M billed at on-demand rate. Using default on-demand (2.0x): 180M * ($0.00110) = $198,000.
- Quarterly true-up: net consumption vs committed across three months; billing adjusted and credits applied in following invoice.

Concessions we can offer for a first-year term (conditional on 12-month commitment):
- Promotional commit discount of 12% on the listed commit rates for first six months.
- Cap on maximum on-demand multiplier at 2.0x for the first contract year.
- Option to purchase an additional "burst block" of reserved tokens at a discounted overage rate to cover predictable events.

I've attached the pricing worksheet (Aurum_Redwood_Pricing_Worksheet.xlsx) that lays out token math and monthly invoice scenarios. If you'd like, we can produce a version with your exact monthly breakdown and a PO-friendly layout.

Next steps: confirm preferred commit tier (50/100/200M), whether you want the initial promotional discount, and if you prefer the capped burst option (1.8x first 20% then 2.0x). Once agreed, I will loop in legal for contract language and send a redline-ready SOW + DocuSign.

Best,

From: aditya_rao@redwood.com

Subject: Fwd: Clarify: volume breakpoints, on-demand overage & true-up process — concession ask

Lauren / Marissa — forwarding Aurum's procurement note and my response. Key points: 120M baseline, realistic spikes to ~300M; they want clear minima, overage rates, and a soft-burst buffer. I proposed standard terms + possible concessions.

Concession asks I'm considering to win the deal:
- 12% promotional discount on commit rates for first 6 months (conditional on 12-month term).
- Cap on on-demand multiplier at 2.0x for year 1.
- Offer a 20% soft-burst buffer reconciled quarterly.

Questions: 1) Are we comfortable with the 75% minimum bill on monthlies for a 12-month agreement? 2) Can we approve the 12% promo (MRR impact modeled in attached worksheet)? 3) Any reason to offer an explicit "burst block" (prepaid burst tokens) at a discounted rate to de-risk overage?

I need an OK or a steer so I can finalize language for legal.

Thanks,
Aditya

From: lauren_bishop@redwood.com
To: aditya_rao@redwood.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com
Date: Sun, 23 May 2027 11:22:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Fwd: Clarify: volume breakpoints, on-demand overage & true-up process — concession ask

Thanks for the summary, Aditya. High level: we should be flexible but protect revenue predictability. My approvals and recommended guardrails below.

Approvals / guidance:
- Approve a promotional commit discount up to 12% for the first 6 months, provided we secure a 12-month term and a minimum monthly bill equal to 75% of committed tokens. Stick with your 75% min.
- Approve cap on on-demand multiplier at 2.0x for contract year 1. Do not go below 1.8x as our baseline economics assume at least that spread.
- Soft-burst buffer: acceptable at 20% per month, but require true-up language that allows for reconciliation at quarter end with clear invoicing cadence.
- Burst block option: good idea. Offer a one-time purchasable burst block (e.g., 50M tokens) at 1.5x committed rate; purchasers can draw down before being billed at on-demand. This product should be optional and sold as an upsell.
- Legal: ensure the contract has: (a) quarterly true-up, (b) explicit minimum-billing floor, (c) definition of "on-demand" and the multipliers, and (d) a cap on promotional discounts. No open-ended credits.

Please proceed to finalize the SOW and send to legal for a redline. Note: include the HubSpot deal id RDW-2027-AURUM-1 in the SOW header and tag the region as US.

Lauren Bishop
Director, Sales Operations
Redwood Inference
